svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif, Apple Color Emoji, Segoe UI Emoji, Noto Color Emoji
svg.title: Life of a change request
svg.desc: Every change request, from Jira, a GitLab or GitHub issue, the chat, a Markdown file or a finding, is filed by the chantier CLI and lands in one Markdown file, 01-intent.md, in 1-inbox. A CR is usually implemented in a pull or merge request (PR/MR). Some CRs do not translate to a PR. The Chief of Staff triages it with you: drop it to 5-trash, send it straight to the backlog when it is automatable with a short spec, write a Change Specification you review until approved, or grill you and record your answers in 02-answers.md before triaging again. A prototype may feed your review: the destination, shown, such as a UI mockup or a vibe-coded app, often made by you, outside this cycle. In 2-backlog you set its priority, P1 to P4. The chantier triage command moves a ready CR to the backlog. On your go, the Chief of Staff opens a batch in 3-requests with chantier open, the Foreman, whose heartbeat loop runs chantier status --refresh, queues the CR and hands it with chantier take to a CR driver, runs it in its own worktree and branch: when the code is unfamiliar, an Investigator maps it before round 1; then rounds of Coder and Inspector until the driver approves the implementation, at most three rounds. Then a rebase, the gate and ship open the PR, so the gate passes on the final head; CI and a Verifier at the pushed head follow, and a red check or a failed verification is a new round. The driver hands back ready, you merge, and chantier order merged moves the CR to 4-archives. With a stacked batch, a Stack driver orders, restacks and ships the PRs, runs the heavy CI once at the top and hands each CR back ready. On your request, at any time of the batch, the Foreman starts a QA driver that uses the head of the default branch as its user would, never an unmerged PR; its findings come back to the intake. The batch has three parts, all started by the Foreman: quality assurance, implementation and release. Once every other CR is merged or cancelled, the Foreman hands the release CR to a Release driver with chantier take; it runs your release procedure and its checks, and asks the Foreman before merging the release PR, which chantier release go allows on your approval or grant. A failed step writes fix-n.md, which becomes a fix CR on your go, unless your grant covers it; the fast track takes up to three fixes per release. A CR driver makes the targeted fix. A fix merges on its own only under your fix grant, an exceptional authorisation for this release's fixes, always bounded by a budget: the Foreman merges it within the granted budget; otherwise you merge it. Either way, the Release driver resumes to finish the release. Once released, the Release driver may monitor the deploys, on package registries, pages and the like, writes retro.md, whose recommendations come back to the intake as a process-improvement CR, and hands back ready; the release CR goes to 4-archives. Once every CR is merged or cancelled, the Foreman runs chantier land: the batch's STATUS.md becomes the exit report, with the final cost; the Foreman sends it as final to the Chief of Staff, who shows you the bilan and the cost, and on your yes runs chantier close, which deletes the batch folder. A blocked driver hands back to the Foreman, which may raise the question to the Chief of Staff, who asks you and sends orders back. A bug found outside the CR's scope goes to the Foreman too, which judges: the driver takes it into the CR, the Foreman raises it to the Chief of Staff, who presents it to you for a decision, or the Foreman files it as a finding in the intake. So each part ends with findings or recommendations back in the intake: often several findings from QA, bugs from implementation, a process-improvement CR from release; from there the loop starts again. At any time, chantier order drop moves a CR to 5-trash, with its work. The chantier CLI gives guidance and feedback to agents and writes a human-readable STATUS.md.
svg.text: Every Change Request (CR) lands in one Markdown file; the CR folder moves and is enriched with prototype, spec and reports.
A CR is usually implemented in a pull or merge request (PR/MR).
Some CRs do not translate to a PR.

g.text: the destination, shown: a UI mockup, a vibe-coded app…
often made by you, outside this cycle
asked by Foreman; may raise to you
merges release PR on release go
chantier CLI gives guidance and feedback to agents, writes human-readable STATUS.md.
At any time: order drop → 5-trash/, with its work.
